title: 地空混合前线推进战
scope: Expands the original air-frontline goal; both Korean and Taiwan theatres, aviation repairs, airfields and HUD requirements remain required. Adds one-human AI-versus-AI observation with zero human combatants required.

confirmed.playerCountInterpretation: Assume 8–12 total human players per team across both roles; larger separate air/ground quotas have not been requested.
roles: Tank company commander: directly drive one tank, command AI platoons through the map
Pilot: fly in the same ongoing battle

company.afterCommandTankLoss: After loss of the controlled tank, the player may take over an owned surviving AI tank; preserve its position, ammunition, damage and vehicle life.
company.whileOwnerFlies: AI continues the last accepted company task while its owner flies; the company remains owned by that player.
company.replacements: Missing company members are replenished in batches at a friendly deployment source. Reinforcement vehicles physically follow a valid route to rejoin; no instant frontline refill.
company.ordersWhileFlying: While flying, the owner can issue simplified move/attack/defend map orders to the same company, while directly controlling only one vehicle.

confirmed.roleSwitchGate: At a friendly deployment area, or after loss of the current vehicle, choose tank/company or aircraft sortie
confirmed.airportLogistics: Light logistics: facilities and transport affect supply functions; no per-round airport stock ledger
confirmed.bridges: Destructible; engineers can repair or construct temporary crossings, and units may seek detours
confirmed.runwayRecovery: Temporary closure of damaged areas; engineer repair accelerated by escorted supply
confirmed.intelligence: Detected contacts shared by the team; lost mobile contacts retain last known position rather than live truth
confirmed.platforms: Desktop priority; simplified mobile graphics with the same complete gameplay and accepted world

friendlyFire.meaning: Friendly units remain physical obstacles and ballistic contacts; disabling friendly damage must not make them transparent.

confirmed.taiwanCoverage: Entire Taiwan main island plus retained mainland coast/Penghu/Kinmen/Matsu in a real1:1 theatre; partial-island options are comparison evidence only.

aiSpectatorMode.teams: Both sides AI-controlled; actual ground/air combat and shared frontline rules
aiSpectatorMode.entry: Separate AI battle observation choice with map and era selection
maps: Full Taiwan main island and retained strait geography
aiSpectatorMode.defaultProposals: Pure observation at1x with free camera, unit follow and tactical map; takeover/pause/speed controls remain optional unconfirmed additions

proposedCoreLoop: Join team and era room, choose a tank company or aircraft and valid deployment point
Ground commander drives the command tank; three AI platoons execute accepted map orders
Ground forces contest connected objectives and protect bridges, engineers and logistics
Pilots intercept hostile aircraft, escort friendly sorties and support actual ground engagements
Successful ground attacks advance the same front for all players; strikes affect actual vehicles and functioning supplies
Recover at friendly zones, service or replace losses, then choose the next role
Resolve readiness/frontline objectives/time limit and reset all round-owned state

companyPolicyProposals.onePersistentCompanySlotPerPlayer: A role change cannot create another full company. Surviving members and orders remain accepted world entities.
companyPolicyProposals.whenPilot: AI continues the last accepted company task while its owner flies; the company remains owned by that player. While flying, the owner can issue simplified move/attack/defend map orders to the same company, while directly controlling only one vehicle.
companyPolicyProposals.commandTankLoss: Offer takeover of an owned surviving AI vehicle after the controlled tank is lost. Reassign command/control role without creating a new tank, refilling ammunition or repairing damage. No surviving unit is reset.
companyPolicyProposals.replacements: Missing company members are replenished in batches at a friendly deployment source. Reinforcement vehicles physically follow a valid route to rejoin; no instant frontline refill. Timing, batch size and travel conditions remain tuning proposals.
companyPolicyProposals.disconnect: AI continues or safely withdraws the same units; reconnect restores company identity, orders, ammo and damage. Team company-slot limits prevent accumulation by joining/leaving.
companyPolicyProposals.manualTank: Map orders address the AI platoons. The player command tank remains under direct control unless an explicit assist is selected.
companyPolicyProposals.combat: Each tank needs its own visibility, aiming, ammunition, damage, mobility and accepted shots. Orders do not directly subtract enemy HP.
companyPolicyProposals.contactPolicy: An attack-area order moves and searches there; an expired map contact is not a live aiming or missile-guidance track.
companyPolicyProposals.followAfterCommanderLoss: Followers hold or defend the last accepted area until a valid replacement/AI leader is assigned; they cannot follow a destroyed vehicle or stale player input.
companyPolicyProposals.controlChanges: Release held triggers and pending input, advance control epoch, preserve unit damage/ammo/fuel and reject stale input from the previous controller.
companyPolicyProposals.strengthExample: 10 alive before loss → 9 surviving AI vehicles after the command tank is destroyed → takeover produces 1 player-controlled tank + 8 AI, still 9 alive. Replacements are separate accepted arrivals.
companyPolicyProposals.commandRole: The command role may move to a survivor; it is not permanently tied to the original command-tank hull. Orders to a platoon affect only its AI-controlled members, preserving the player direct-driving choice.
companyPolicyProposals.noSurvivors: With no survivor available, ground re-entry needs a valid deployment/replacement process; exact recovery timing remains a tuning proposal.
companyPolicyProposals.replacementReservations: Reserve company/platoon vacancies for incoming units, counting survivors and accepted arrivals toward the initial ten-vehicle cap; reroute or hold reinforcements if a route is cut. An arrival cannot reset survivors or charge the same loss twice.

deploymentProposals.ground: Road-distance candidate staging anchors1200m from the active road battle reference, with source-path gaps blocked. Native terrain, protected egress,10 separate parking footprints and supply gates still require authoring.
deploymentProposals.groundTravelTarget: Roughly 2–5 minutes to first contact, using actual 1:1 route distances rather than compressed map scale.
deploymentProposals.air: Retain the four airport candidates and rear airborne options; take-off/landing/loadout checks remain necessary.
deploymentProposals.queue: Reserve clear, nonoverlapping vehicle/formation pads; no 10-tank spawn pile or creation inside enemy-held ground.
deploymentProposals.fieldReturn: Switching roles requires the accepted friendly deployment condition; opening the map is not a free escape from combat.
deploymentProposals.companyContinuation: Role changes and vehicle losses must not silently delete the surviving company from the battle.

frontlineProposals.groundCapture: Eligible player tanks, AI combat vehicles and infantry physically contest adjacent objectives; infantry help consolidate positions.
frontlineProposals.rateCap: Cap capture speed benefits from multiple members so ten tanks do not instantly flip an objective.
frontlineProposals.bridges: Deck damage changes actual passability. AI stops, reroutes or waits for engineers. Temporary bridges require authored valid banks, approaches and load classes.
frontlineProposals.engineers: A real engineer unit must reach the work area and complete accepted repair progress; an offscreen countdown alone does not prove a repaired crossing.
frontlineProposals.logistics: Truck arrival and facility condition maintain abstract supply availability; individual vehicle ammunition/fuel remain accepted quantities.
frontlineProposals.targets: Authored military task compounds and moving units, not automatic designation of every real civilian building as a target.

populationEnvelope.counting: Command tanks are already included in the ten tanks per company. Do not add the human-driven tank again.
populationEnvelope.roleChangeWorstCase: Companies may remain active while their owners fly; aircraft and surviving companies must fit the same measured budget.
populationEnvelope.supportForces: The old air-only 36-ground-vehicles-per-team draft is superseded. Infantry, APCs, artillery, air defence, logistics and engineers still need explicit combined-mode budgets.
populationEnvelope.simulation: One accepted simulation and combat result for desktop and mobile. Client graphics settings cannot remove enemy units or change fighting/capture outcomes.
populationEnvelope.performanceStatus: A local release30-unit ground world sustained approximately20Hz; the observer stream used approximately1.51MB/s of UTF-8 JSON before transport overhead. No maximum8–12-human-per-team/240-company-tank-plus-support, WAN or complete mobile gameplay benchmark has passed.

supportForceProposalPerTeam.status: Initial combined-mode proposal, not a measured performance or final balance claim

populationEnvelope.supportForceProposalNotes: Supports the front even when no human selects a ground company. The 120-company-tank-per-team maximum is additional to these support forces.

implementationBoundary.matchScenario: Add a separate combined-frontline scenario identity and version. Existing Casual/Historical gameplay modes are physics/rule profiles, not this scenario.
implementationBoundary.ownership: Separate player connection, controlled vehicle, company and platoon identities. AI units cannot be implemented as fake network players.
implementationBoundary.handover: One active driver per unit and one directly controlled vehicle per player; control handover does not reset ammo, damage or life identity.
implementationBoundary.personalSpawnPoints: The legacy aircraft personal spawn-point gate conflicts with the confirmed no-personal-currency rule and cannot be reused unchanged in this scenario.
implementationBoundary.terrainAndContacts: Rendered roads, runways, bridge decks, ground contacts and weapon impacts need one geometry/height convention. Native geometry query support alone is not complete combat integration.
implementationBoundary.eraCatalog: Validate ground and aircraft variants, weapons, pods, sensors and air defence together; current type labels and universal loadout menus are insufficient.
implementationBoundary.implementationBase: The implementation worktree descends from verified f3c6d88/core212 and verified030e8cb aircraft-era fix. Ground/HUD feature096f2cffc9e4bb76029d9db5514ec86327a3726c is retained; shared-air foundation commit is 08719fd951464f07ff3d2cccfaff1c52cf45fcdd. The older design worktree6799e22/core211 is not a release base.
implementationBoundary.legacyPersonalSpawnPoints: Remove the personal p.sp eligibility/cost path for this combined scenario; keep individual vehicle ammo/fuel accounting and shared team readiness.
implementationBoundary.sharedGameAssistance: Retain the user-requested Space+R ACM on all existing radar-equipped types. This game control feature does not imply modern radar range, pulse-Doppler capability or missile compatibility for older aircraft.
implementationBoundary.visibilityOverlays: Scenario contact/discovery rules gate both map and 3D aids in either physics profile; existing Casual all-enemy hints must not bypass discovery. Stale map contacts are not live radar/seeker guidance.
implementationBoundary.combatScope: The initial combined scenario may reuse existing accepted vehicle damage rules. Newly authored bridge/runway surfaces must have consistent visible and physical geometry. A full vehicle visible-triangle migration remains a separate, explicitly verified integration claim.
implementationBoundary.projectileIdentity: Shots and guided weapons retain the original unit/life target reference. Changing a player controlled vehicle cannot retarget an old projectile onto the new vehicle.
implementationBoundary.friendlyDamage: Suppress allied damage and loss charging through the same accepted hit/blast path, while retaining physical vehicle contact, line-of-sight occlusion and projectile contacts. Check bombs, shells, missiles and secondary effects; do not remove allied hulls from collision queries.
implementationBoundary.observer: Observers are separate from team combat participants and company owners. Full spectator information cannot feed AI perception or leak into the playable team contact channel. A single observer can start an AI battle; zero human combatants does not stop its simulation.

currentCodeEvidence.finding: Legacy Player retains its single-vehicle/life state. The separate implemented FrontlineHub now owns persistent companies, independent native unit lives and control epochs; AI units are not fake Player records.

Legacy Room remains separate. FrontlineHub now owns shared ground/air scenario rooms, observers, persistent companies, independent unit lives/control epochs, resources, readiness and one C2 objective; full logistics/infrastructure remain absent.
Legacy deployment still charges personal p.sp and creates an AirSeat. The new scenario uses its separate FrontlineHub DeployAir path and shared team readiness, without personal currency.
Aircraft damage data uses skin/part boxes and imported loadout definitions; this is not evidence of completed native visible-surface combat integration.

The real legacy DeployScreen->deploy_air->air_spawned->enterAircraftOnline skeleton is preserved. New FrontlineHub/actual client now add independent same-world ground/air units, runway/rear-air starts and shared gun/bomb/rocket contacts/resources; full airfield service is still missing.

Legacy room max still clamps to16 total humans. The new frontline domain separately enforces12 human slots/team and persistent company limits, but requested maximum population and performance remain unverified.

The reproduced missing-T.era eligibility bug was fixed locally by030e8cb: actual online UI/server aircraft metadata-year admission is checked before state/SP mutation. Full variant/store/sensor era certification is still unfinished and this fix is not a deployment claim.

Legacy advance_aircraft advances damage rather than flight dynamics. New scenario aircraft use the unchanged flight_core.wasm212 through per-aircraft isolated wasmi Store/Instance; native ground motion and basic autonomous air AI share the accepted world.

Actual versioned shared ground/air room/observer/company/unit-life/control-epoch domain, ground and aircraft deployment/input/return, survivor takeover, ownership-preserving role changes, orders during flight, readiness and reconnect/leave handling are integrated through Lobby/socket wrappers.

Actual native tracked plants, shared terrain, aiming, finite mounted main-cannon ammunition and ballistic legacy module/crew contacts now interact with aircraft gun/bomb/rocket rounds and accepted aircraft skin/part-box damage. This is not visible-triangle combat migration or complete secondary-weapons/infantry support.

Canonical native/rendered elevation, patches, pads and rotated runway grading are shared. C2/centre:C2-local-test1.8km remains the only enabled ground front. B-E/R-W2600m game-expanded runway/rear-air starts enable bounded aircraft tests; real expansion or full theatre acceptance is not claimed.

Actual local client now renders authoritative ground/air units and allows observer/company/pilot controls; ground distant visual LOD leaves native state intact. Prior ground browser14 functional assertions passed with overall screenshot-timeout failure retained; new one-browser mixed three-scenario QA is pending.

Grouped aircraft ammo/stores and current-consumption fuel endurance retain72 prior actual browser HUD checks. New shared mode now consumes accepted server aircraft resources; new mixed browser verification is pending and airfield service remains missing.

Commit08719fd951464f07ff3d2cccfaff1c52cf45fcdd:24 source-derived aircraft profiles, unchanged core212 per-instance Store, safe input timeout, monotonic ownership/seq, metadata25-year admission, persistent store-release cooldown and separated spatial air starts. Source profiles are not complete historical loadout/sensor or model-fidelity certification.

acceptanceGates: Two real clients control tank companies and aircraft concurrently in one server battle
Every commander sees the accepted three-platoon membership and can issue move/attack/defend orders only to authorised units
AI vehicles physically move, aim, fire, take damage, lose mobility and interact with terrain/bridges rather than scripted outcome bars
Company and vehicle state survive valid role changes, command-tank loss, disconnect and reconnect without cloning or resets
Takeover of a surviving AI tank preserves its actual position, ammunition, damage and life; company strength reflects losses instead of resetting to ten
Actual tanks/infantry capture and advance at multiple connected fronts; planes affect the same fighting
Runway and bridge damage, engineering recovery and supply affect shared passability and service availability
Aircraft UI shows accepted ammo and fuel endurance, with both valid airborne and field starts
Era restrictions and shared pool enforced server-side for ground, air, weapons and sensors
Playable Korean and Taiwan real-data maps, including sea transport/beachheads in Taiwan, at the agreed scale
Measured worst-case AI, rendering and replication performance; mobile retains the same gameplay
Complete round victory, readiness charging and clean reset at the agreed duration
Remaining aircraft ground control-surface animation and separately authorised asset repairs verified against actual models

One human enters AI observation alone; both AI teams actually move/fight, use accepted ammunition/damage/service and advance the same front without human State packets; camera controls do not create a player vehicle or command a team.
openDesignItems: Physical reinforcement timing, batch size and source/deployment route validation; player policy already confirmed
Ground staging/capture-node revisions after road/bridge connectivity and native terrain checks
Matched variant/weapon/sensor profiles and candidate era-room review
Support-unit population and measured server/client budgets
Whole-Taiwan theatre active battle areas, streaming terrain and actual sea/land logistics

designEvidence.limits: The geography/staging/airport research artifacts remain surveys, not complete vehicle-specific playability evidence. Separate actual runtime validation now exists for the enabled C2 ground prototype only; full theatre/air/infrastructure acceptance remains open.
